title: Linux Administration: Services, Logs & Safe Recovery
purpose: Eight offline guest-administration lessons. Learn a controlled change, service lifecycle and startup, ownership, local logs, rotation and incident recovery. Sequence is guidance; completion is self-reviewed and unscored.
prerequisites: Paths, file copying, basic permissions, text filters, nano and process inspection. Lesson 1 teaches quoting, exit status, && and privileged redirection. No preceding scripting batch is required. This separate image grants learner full guest-root sudo; the older images remain unprivileged.
coverage: Partial LPIC-2 v4.5 202.1 systemd administration; LPIC-1 v5.0 108.2 local logging, 104.5 ownership/access, 107.1 limited-account inspection, 101.3 controlled reboot and introductory shell reinforcement. No full objectives, SysV boot, rescue/GRUB, network logging, general account lifecycle or verified assessment.

entries.description: Inspect guest privileges and make one reversible configuration edit.
objectives: LPIC-1 103.1/103.4 introductory shell reinforcement; preparation for 105.2
troubleshooting: Read the exact unit and guest path before sudo. A failure is evidence; preserve output before changing anything.
The lab service ends after 120 seconds. An inactive/timeout state after that bound is expected; inspect timestamps before diagnosing a new fault.
If the console or guest breaks, use the app Stop control. Resume requires a clean disk; confirmed Reset retains the old generation.
cleanup: Keep original.conf as evidence; optional cleanup removes only change.conf.before after successful restoration.
materials: Guest-only administration: learner has passwordless full root through sudo. Root can override every guest-side teaching limit. No host commands, NIC, shares or clipboard.
Each lesson has a separate disk session and dormant fixture. Begin with a fresh session for the stated initial fault; Resume retains your changes. All paths below are inside the guest.
observations: Identity/sudo policy, failure status, configuration diff and final comparison.
questions: Why can a pipeline with sudo tee write a root-owned file while sudo printf > file can still fail?
limitations: Do not change login/PAM, sudoers, bootloader, essential mounts, networking or unrelated units. Scope repairs to ll-* units and /etc/learning-lab or /var/log/learning-lab.

Lab workers run as locked non-login ll-service, at most 120 seconds, 64 MiB memory, 8 tasks, 20% of one CPU and 1 MiB per-file limit. They emit only a few lines. Root can remove these limits; they are not a boundary against guest administrators.
Guest files and self-review records are excluded from profile backups/exports. Resume boots disk files, not RAM/jobs. No public image release or automatic assessment is implied.
